description: Mentors describe him from his teens as unusually effective at getting what he wants; Graham calls him 'extremely effective' and a person of 'force of will'.
notes: Graham (2006-2014), Thiel (2016) and Andreessen. Mostly from beneficiaries of his favor network; discount for halo.

description: Closes outsized deals, often before a product justifies them: carrier deals for Loopt, a $1B nonprofit pledge, Microsoft billions, Stargate. Friends and critics agree on this.
notes: Witnesses: Shear, Chesky, Nadella, the documented round record. No source disputes it.

description: Pushes founders and himself to 'add a zero' and frames projects as civilization-scale (AGI for all, fusion, universal identity).
notes: Chesky (M to B), Varden Labs, Andreessen ('ambition up 10x'), Graham ('make the whole future').

description: Builds wide networks of people who owe him or depend on a shared project, then activates them under pressure, as in the Nov 2023 staff letter and Microsoft offer.
notes: Same behavior read positively by allies and as board capture by critics (McCauley, Toner). The ouster audit frames it as conditional coalition management, not proof of planned dependence.

description: Several named insiders say he told different people different things or withheld information from the board. The board fired him for not being 'consistently candid'.
notes: Toner (2024, on record), Murati and McCauley (2026 testimony, press-reported), Sutskever memo (reported). Unadjudicated; WilmerHale found conduct did not mandate removal. Toner's Loopt-era claims are quarantined.

description: Avoids direct confrontation and defers hard calls, then makes sudden clean breaks; he admits conflict-aversion 'caused great pain'.
notes: Self-admission (2026) and Toner (2024), plus Murati (2026, reported). 2026 counterpoint: 'very happy to fire people quickly'.

description: Shows little public distress in crises: terse warm posts during the firing, measured Senate testimony, a reflective rather than vengeful response to the 2026 attack.
notes: This is displayed composure only; see 'Contained private anxiety'.

description: Privately anxious: his mother describes 'cyber-chondria' and stress kept inside; he calls his past self 'very anxious, unhappy' and reports poor sleep since ChatGPT.
notes: Mother (2016), himself (2024 podcast), himself (2025 sleep remark, snippet-level).

description: Accelerates AI and techno-optimism publicly while preparing for catastrophe (prepper stockpile, doom quotes, the 2026 slowdown).
notes: Thiel ('optimist yet a survivalist'), his own 2015-2016 quotes, his own 2023-2026 statements.

description: Works at a punishing pace from his teens: scurvy at 19, 'strapped to a time bomb' tempo, relentless list-driven productivity.
notes: New Yorker 2016 observer, his productivity essay, 2025-26 interview snippets.

description: Says management was his 'chief weakness' at Loopt and avoids one-on-ones; colleagues describe chaos and impatience with the ineffective.
notes: Self (2016), Murati written feedback (2022 exhibit), BI anonymous staff (2023).

description: Keeps open lines to staff and founders (open Slack, personal number, drop-in office hours) and is called the 'Michael Jordan of listening'.
notes: YC founders (2016), BI staff (2023), Coogan via Bloomberg (2024). Mostly beneficiaries.

description: Writes in short lowercase posts and directives ('Buy the computers') and uses numbered essays as his main self-narrative.
notes: Constant style across about two decades of X/HN/blog records.

description: Takes large personal bets: dropping out at 19, $375M into fusion, 'all my liquid net worth' into Helion and Retro, $500B infrastructure.
notes: Documented actions, not testimony; counted as independent dated decisions.

description: Critics say he launched or committed to things before overseers knew: ChatGPT on Twitter, Startup Fund ownership, Helion deals, YC Research despite partners.
notes: Toner (2024), Zilis (2026, press-reported), Levy via New Yorker 2016 on YC Research. Unadjudicated.

description: Staff rallied to him in very large numbers while board members and senior peers broke with him.
notes: The ouster audit cautions that signatures reflect incentives and outside options, not just trust.

trait: Concede the process, not personal fault
description: Under pressure he makes quick procedural concessions (pause Sky, release NDAs, restore GPT-4o, 'he's right') while admitting little personal wrongdoing.
notes: The 2025 'Reflections' and 2026 blog are partial exceptions that do admit personal failures.

description: Answers attacks with his own dated documents and posts (Musk email dumps, the Sky timeline, essays) rather than in interviews.
notes: Based on OpenAI and Altman publications; interpretation is the profile's synthesis.

description: Each exit leads to a bigger role: Loopt sale to YC presidency, YC to OpenAI CEO, firing to return with a friendlier board.
notes: Pattern over three episodes; the YC exit's framing is contested.

description: Wants to spread AI's gains widely (basic income, American Equity Fund, Worldcoin, 'no one should have the ring') while pursuing concentrated scale.
notes: Own essays across 2016-2026, plus the funded study and Giving Pledge.

description: Relies on a few long-standing allies: Graham, Brockman, Thiel, brothers Jack and Max, cousin Serralta, and Chesky and Lehane in 2023.
notes: No retrieved roster beyond these nodes; Graham relationship later cooled.

description: Shifts political alignment pragmatically: Democratic donor, then $1M to Trump's inauguration and a White House Stargate launch, then 'politically homeless'.
notes: Donations VERIFIED; staff dissent REPORTED. No 2026 midterm donations.

description: Critics say people who crossed him faced consequences (the push to remove Toner, freezing out Murati, subpoenas to critic nonprofits).
notes: Toner (on record), McCauley (2026, press-reported), Hao (anonymous). One-sided and unproven.

description: Reads the room and persuades quickly ('Jedi mind tricks', 'king of the cannibals'), calibrating his message to each audience.
notes: Graham (2008-2009), an unnamed tech executive (New Yorker 2026), testimony coverage. The skill is uncontested; its use is contested.

description: Signals without committing in ways that are hard to pin down: the 'her' post, 'no equity in OpenAI', a co-drafted tweet during the crisis.
notes: Readings of intent are contested; the posts themselves are VERIFIED.

description: Calls for AI licensing in public while OpenAI opposed specific bills (SB 1047) and threatened to leave the EU.
notes: Ex-employee SB 1047 letter (VERIFIED document); UCL remarks and walk-back.

description: Keeps his relationship and family largely private: the relationship 'fairly under wraps', a private-Instagram wedding, the child's name undisclosed.
notes: BI via Advocate (2024), NBC (2024), absence of name across 2025-26 sources.
